concerns: The EEG signals were not recorded while subjects viewed the cluttered images or answered the VQA questions; EEG trials and images are paired only at the category level, so the claimed EEG-guided ROI benefit is not demonstrated under the actual inference conditions.

Short-phrase VQA answers are scored by GPT-5.5 without reported inter-annotator agreement, human calibration, or validation against independent labels, leaving the headline accuracy gains dependent on an unvalidated automated evaluator.

The real-world applicability claim for VR/AR is overextended because the evaluation uses synthetic category-matched EEG-image pairing and generated cluttered scenes rather than live perceptual EEG routing during visual search.
scholarly_quality.concise_summary: While the framework and efficiency metrics are systematically presented, the study's construct validity is undermined by synthetic category-level pairing of EEG data with artificial cluttered images, as well as reliance on uncalibrated LLM evaluation for open-ended VQA answers. Consequently, scientific certainty regarding real EEG-guided efficiency benefits remains unestablished.

BrainFocus: EEG-Guided ROI Selection for Efficient
Vision-Language Models
Yihui Peng* , Guorui Lu* ,Student Member, IEEE, Qinyu Chen ,Member, IEEE
Abstract—Vision-language models (VLMs) achieve strong visual
question answering (VQA) performance, but processing large
cluttered images is computationally expensive when only a small
region is relevant. Electroencephalography (EEG) signals, which
capture human neural responses to visual stimuli, can provide a
human-derived semantic cue about the region of interest (ROI).
However, EEG-guided visual category decoding remains imperfect,
making direct ROI routing unreliable. In this work, we propose
BrainFocus, a reliable EEG-guided efficient VLM framework
for VQA. An EEG classifier predicts a target category, and a
YOLO detector localizes the matching ROI. The VLM receives
the cropped ROI only when both predictions pass confidence
thresholds;

are imperfect, unconditional cropping can result in a poor
cropping effect, and excessive incorrect cropping will remove
the necessary visual evidence needed for VQA. We therefore
employ a sequential confidence-gated fallback strategy, which
includes two gates: EEG gate and ROI gate. The EEG gate will
first evaluate each request. If ceeg < τeeg, Stage 2 is skipped
and the full image is sent directly to Stage 3. Otherwise, Stage 2
searches for a detection matching the predicted WNID. The
cropped ROI is fed to Stage 3 only when a matching box
exists and croi ≥τ roi, while all other requests use the full-
image fallback. Thus, every request can reach Stage 3, whereas
crop routing requires both confidence gates to pass.

blocking_reasons: The EEG signals were not recorded while subjects viewed the cluttered images or answered the VQA questions; EEG trials and images are paired only at the category level, so the claimed EEG-guided ROI benefit is not demonstrated under the actual inference conditions.

Short-phrase VQA answers are scored by GPT-5.5 without reported inter-annotator agreement, human calibration, or validation against independent labels, leaving the headline accuracy gains dependent on an unvalidated automated evaluator.

The real-world applicability claim for VR/AR is overextended because the evaluation uses synthetic category-matched EEG-image pairing and generated cluttered scenes rather than live perceptual EEG routing during visual search.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The threshold calibration objective was crop reliability and acceptance rate, not the final VQA accuracy metric.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: End-to-end VQA accuracy on test sets, scored by exact/synonym matching and GPT-5.5 for short-phrase answers, plus token and FLOPs reductions.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Confidence thresholds were selected on held-out validation trials to maximize non-fallback rate subject to precision at least 0.97, where precision is defined by EEG category correctness and target IoU.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims of real-world applicability (e.g., VR/AR) are substantially overextended given that EEG signals were collected during isolated ImageNet stimuli viewing and later synthetic-category-matched to separate images, bypassing actual eye-movement or cognitive visual search dynamics in cluttered scenes.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluation across 15 subjects and three Qwen3.5-VL model sizes measures VQA accuracy, token reduction, and FLOPs. A critical limitation is that the cluttered images are synthetically generated and question answers for short phrases are judged by an automated LLM evaluator (GPT-5.5) without inter-annotator validation or human calibration against false acceptances.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The test scoring metric was not directly optimized in the threshold calibration step.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: VQA accuracy on test sets evaluated via exact match and GPT-5.5 scoring, alongside token and FLOPs reduction.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Confidence threshold tuning on validation trials maximizing non-fallback rate under an IoU and category accuracy constraint.

primary.limitations: The authors acknowledge domain differences between real and generated images and declining coverage at higher class counts, but fail to address the core artificiality of category-level EEG-image matching versus live perceptual EEG routing.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology pipelines an EEG classifier (MLP on differential entropy features), a YOLO detector, confidence gating calibrated on validation trials, and a frozen VLM. However, EEG trials and images are paired artificially at the category level rather than recording EEG from subjects actually viewing the target cluttered images or questions.
primary.quality_rationale: While the framework and efficiency metrics are systematically presented, the study's construct validity is undermined by synthetic category-level pairing of EEG data with artificial cluttered images, as well as reliance on uncalibrated LLM evaluation for open-ended VQA answers. Consequently, scientific certainty regarding real EEG-guided efficiency benefits remains unestablished.
primary.scoped_contribution: BrainFocus proposes a sequential confidence-gated pipeline that uses EEG category predictions and a fine-tuned YOLO detector to crop regions of interest before VLM inference, falling back to full-image processing when confidence is insufficient.

scholarly_quality.rationale: While the framework and efficiency metrics are systematically presented, the study's construct validity is undermined by synthetic category-level pairing of EEG data with artificial cluttered images, as well as reliance on uncalibrated LLM evaluation for open-ended VQA answers. Consequently, scientific certainty regarding real EEG-guided efficiency benefits remains unestablished.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors acknowledge domain differences between real and generated images and declining coverage at higher class counts, but fail to address the core artificiality of category-level EEG-image matching versus live perceptual EEG routing.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
